subject: Extracting percent raster pixel is covered by polygon - unexpected results

messages.author: c3006bd7c5a7a468
messages.subject: Extracting percent raster pixel is covered by polygon - unexpected results
parts:
Hello all,

I am finding some unexpected results when trying to extract the percent each pixel in my raster layer is covered by water (polygons from a shape file).

I am using the extract() function (i.e. extract(raster, water, cellnumbers=T, weights=T, normalizeWeights=F, df=T)).  The resulting data look 95% correct but sometimes seems to be identifying cells as being covered with water that are not and identifying pixels that have very little water as being nearly completely covered.

Am I doing something wrong? 

My notes and reproducible code are below.  Any suggestions/thoughts are greatly appreciated! 

Thank you!
Eric



#packages
library(raster)
library(rgdal)
library(rgeos)
library(leaflet)
library(maptools)
library(plyr)
library(mapview)

#install packages that are not yet installed
# install.packages("raster")
# install.packages("rgdal")
# install.packages("rgeos")
# install.packages("leaflet")
# install.packages("maptools")
# install.packages("mapview")

#read in data
# raster layer
raster <- raster("raster.tif")  #raster layer
raster[raster>0] <- 1:length(raster)  #recode raster layer so that colors appear nicely

# water polygon layer
water <- readOGR("water.shp")  #water polygon

#take a look at the layers (if you wish)
leaflet() %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addRasterImage(raster, group="raster") %>%
  addPolygons(data=spTransform(water, CRS("+init=epsg:4326")), weight=2, group="water") %>%
  addLayersControl(overlayGroups=c("raster", "water"))


#extract the percent water that covers each pixel (i.e. my expectation is the weight column will be coded in this way: 100% pixel covered by water = 1, 0% pixel covered by water = 0 )
per.cov <- extract(raster, water, cellnumbers=T, weights=T, normalizeWeights=F, df=T)


#because there appear to be multiple polygons that are over the same pixel there are pixel duplicates in the resulting data frame
#this sums the weights (i.e. polygon 1 covers 1% of a pixel and polygon 2 covers 3% of the same pixel.  This code assigns 4% to the percent coverage of that pixel.)
per.cov.tot <- ddply(per.cov, "cell", function(x) c(rast.value=sum(x$raster)/length(x$raster), weight=sum(x$weight)))

#color pixels identified with water by the percentage they are covered by water
#print("NOTICE THAT SOME PIXELS NOT COVERED IN WATER ARE FLAGGED WITH BEING COVERED WITH WATER")
raster.water=raster #copy raster
raster.water[raster.water>0]=NA  #set all raster values to NA
raster.water[per.cov.tot$cell]=per.cov.tot$weight
#take a look at the layers (if you wish)
leaflet() %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addRasterImage(raster.water, group="waterIdentified", opacity=0.99) %>%
#  addRasterImage(raster, group="raster") %>%
  addPolygons(data=spTransform(water, CRS("+init=epsg:4326")), weight=5, group="water") %>%
  addLayersControl(overlayGroups=c("raster", "water", "waterIdentified"))

#id pixels that have over 90% of water
print("NOTICE THAT SOME PIXELS HAVING VERY LITTLE WATER ARE FLAGGED AS BEING MORE THAN 90% COVERED WITH WATER (ESP. ON THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE FIGURE")
raster.water=raster #copy raster
raster.water[raster.water>0]=NA  #set all raster values to NA
raster.water[per.cov.tot$cell[per.cov.tot$weight>.9]]=1000
#take a look at the layers (if you wish)
leaflet() %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addRasterImage(raster.water, group="waterIdentified", opacity=0.99, color="red") %>%
#  addRasterImage(raster, group="raster") %>%
  addPolygons(data=spTransform(water, CRS("+init=epsg:4326")), weight=5, group="water") %>%
  addLayersControl(overlayGroups=c("raster", "water", "waterIdentified"))

parts:
HI Eric,
I think your analysis is doing what you want, but something is just getting messed up somewhere in leaflet when you display it. I am not familiar with leaflet so I really don't know what it could be, but when I run your code and make a plot with base R things seem to line up just fine. Your leaflet plot looks like it has extra cells highlighted for some reason. Attached are the plots and here is the code I used to make mine:

plot(raster.water)
plot(water,add=TRUE)

Katie
